This week, I had the honor of spending time with Lincoln and Parker Moss, and their truly amazing mom Kelly.  They drove from Salem to our nation’s Capitol to tell me about their beloved brother and son, Weston Moss.

Weston was 12. A proud Boy Scout. Loved Super Mario and Legos. Dreamed of designing games at Nintendo. He was an artist who shared his beautiful art with the world.

For his 11th birthday, Weston skipped presents and instead donated 500 LEGO sets to kids fighting cancer at the Jimmy Fund Clinic.

Even while battling a rare bone cancer called Ewing Sarcoma, Wes never stopped thinking of other kids in the fight. In his final days, he had one more wish: that we carry on his mission of ending cancer as we know it and making life better for everyone one of us who is blessed to be living it. 

That’s how Weston’s Big Wish was born.

This morning, I was in Salem with Weston’s amazingly resilient dad James and his loving grandmother Donna at the Salem Lions Race Against Childhood Cancer — neighbors, some meeting the Moss family for the first time, showing up for a truly remarkable boy who gave his all to others.

That’s the living legacy and blessed soul of Weston Moss. That’s Salem. That’s New Hampshire. 

I will never stop fighting to make Weston’s Big Wish a reality: more federal funding for research, kinder treatments, and more joy for every kid facing what Wes faced.

May God bless Weston Moss and the entire Moss family.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ 🙏
